identity.title: Linear filament and nested cluster evolution tomography (LANCET): I. Capture the evolution of dense gas in 14-parsec filament G316.8

paper_type_evidence.loc: Linear filament and nested cluster evolution tomography (LANCET)
paper_type_evidence.quote: The *Linear filament and nested cluster evolution tomography* (LANCET) project mapped the entire G316.8 filament with the Atacama Compact Array (ACA) at 1.3 mm, achieving $6\ensuremath{''}$ (0.08 pc) resolution over $26.7$ arcmin$^2$ (17.1 pc$^2$).
In this first paper of the series, we processed and analyzed the Atacama Compact Array (ACA) 7m continuum data and combined them with *Herschel* and APEX data as zero spacings.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute and fit Column Density Probability Distribution Functions (N-PDFs)

method.value: Subtract uniform foreground/background column density measured in a 5'x5' box, bin normalized logarithmic column density eta = ln(N_H2 / <N_H2>) with 0.1 dex bins for quiet and active regions, and fit a piecewise lognormal + 1 or 2 power-law tail (PLT) model using MCMC.

evidence.quote: We removed a uniform $N^{\rm bkg}_{\rm H_2} = 7 \times 10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$ throughout the image.

evidence.quote: We removed a uniform $N^{\rm bkg}_{\rm H_2} = 7 \times 10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$ throughout the image.
As suggested by (cite: Schneider2015a), the bin size of 0.1 dex provides the best compromise between resolving small features in the N-PDF and avoiding low pixel statistics.

findings_qualitative.value: Dendrogram trees with multilevel branching occur only in the intermediate and evolved subregions, whereas the young subregion contains only isolated, nonhierarchical leaf structures.

evidence.quote: Trees that exhibit multilevel branching host leaves exclusively from the intermediate and evolved subregions, whereas leaves from the young subregion occur only in isolated, nonhierarchical trees.

findings_qualitative.value: Across the evolutionary sequence from young to evolved, gas is progressively concentrated into sub-parsec dense structures, reflected by increasing maximum fragment mass, broadening fragment mass distributions, and rising dense-gas fraction.

evidence.quote: The more physically meaningful evolutionary signature is therefore the increasing dynamic range of fragment masses, as reflected by the progressively broader mass distributions in Fig. 8.

Along the sequence young to intermediate to evolved, the maximum fragment mass and the regional dense-gas mass fraction both increase, indicating progressive concentration of mass into compact (sub-parsec) structures.

claims.hypothesis: As a massive filamentary molecular cloud evolves from an infrared-dark stage through MYSOs to an HII region stage, molecular gas is progressively assembled and concentrated into hierarchical sub-parsec dense fragments.
claims.experiment: Mapped the 14-pc G316.8 filament with a 118-pointing ACA 7m 1.3 mm mosaic combined with Herschel and APEX/ArTéMiS data, and extracted hierarchical structures across the young, intermediate, and evolved subregions using astrodendro.
claims.result: The young region hosts only nonhierarchical leaves while intermediate and evolved regions show multilevel trees; maximum fragment mass grows from 8 to 160 to 490 M_sun and the regional dense-gas mass fraction rises from 0.4% to 2.3% to 9.6%.
claims.finding: Structural hierarchy strengthens and an increasingly large fraction of cloud mass becomes locked into compact sub-parsec fragments as star formation progresses.

evidence.loc: Linear filament and nested cluster evolution tomography (LANCET)
evidence.quote: From young to intermediate to evolved, the maximum fragment mass increases from 8 to 160 to 490 $M_\odot$, while the dense-gas mass fraction ($>0.5$ g cm$^{-2}$) rises from $0.4\%$ to $2.3\%$ to $9.6\%$.
Trees that exhibit multilevel branching host leaves exclusively from the intermediate and evolved subregions, whereas leaves from the young subregion occur only in isolated, nonhierarchical trees.

claims.hypothesis: The column density probability distribution function (N-PDF) evolves from a simpler gravity-dominated profile in quiescent gas to a broader distribution with a flatter primary power-law tail and a secondary high-density tail in evolved, feedback-affected gas.
claims.experiment: Constructed foreground/background-subtracted N-PDFs from the 6.2'' multi-resolution column density map for the quiet and active parts of G316.8 and fit lognormal + power-law tail models with MCMC.
claims.result: The lognormal dispersion in the active region (sigma = 1.17) is twice that of the quiet region (sigma = 0.59); the quiet region fits a single PLT (s_1 = -1.20) with a cutoff at eta = 2.80, whereas the active region shows a flatter first PLT (s_1 = -1.00) and a steep second PLT (s_2 = -7.18) above eta = 3.15.
claims.finding: More evolved and active star-forming regions accumulate more gas at high densities and show flattened primary power-law tails likely shaped by stellar feedback compression.

evidence.quote: At the high-density regime, the south N-PDF is well described by two PLTs. The first one has a slope of about $-1.0$ and steepens to about $-7.2$ at the break point of $\eta=3.14$ or $2\times10^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$.

However, the northern quiet part is better described by a one-PLT model with a hard cutoff at $\eta=2.80$ or $1\times10^{23}$ cm$^{-2}$ and a slightly steeper PLT slope of $-1.2$ than in the active part.

claims.hypothesis: Small-scale density contrast increases systematically with evolutionary stage along the filament.
claims.experiment: Computed the wavelet-based Delta-variance spectrum on the multi-resolution column density map across lags from 0.04 to 2.04 pc and fit a double power-law over 0.1-0.9 pc for each subregion.
claims.result: The small-scale Delta-variance slope alpha_1 decreases monotonically from 2.7 (young) to 1.9 (intermediate) to 1.5 (evolved), and the large-scale slope alpha_2 decreases from 2.3 to 2.1 to 1.4.
claims.finding: Shallower Delta-variance slopes in more evolved regions demonstrate systematically increasing small-scale structure and density contrast as gravity and accretion assemble dense structures.

evidence.quote: For the evolved subregion, the DPL has a small-scale slope of 1.5 and a large-scale slope of 1.4. For the intermediate subregion, they are as steep as 1.9 and 2.1. For the young subregion, they are even steeper at 2.7 and 2.3.
ii) The slope seems to systematically flatten with age: steepest for the young, flatter for the intermediate, and flattest for the evolved.

why_this_data.value: G316.8 is a single 14-pc linear filament at uniform distance (2.8 kpc) containing three contiguous subregions of ~10,000 M_sun each that span young, intermediate, and evolved stages, eliminating distance and environmental biases present in Galactic-wide surveys.

evidence.loc: Linear filament and nested cluster evolution tomography (LANCET)
evidence.quote: The G316.8 filament provides an excellent controlled case: a 14-parsec, nearly linear structure comprising three contiguous subregions with comparable molecular gas reservoirs (each $\sim\!10{,}000$ $M_\odot$), yet spanning a clear evolutionary sequence

why_this_method.value: Combining Herschel and APEX/ArTéMiS with ACA 7m data via multi-resolution SED fitting and J-comb uv combination preserves 6'' resolution to pinpoint dense fragments while recovering large-scale flux and eliminating interferometric negative bowls.

evidence.loc: Multi-resolution temperature and column density images
evidence.quote: To this end, we did not simply smooth all images to the coarsest resolution but instead made full use of their intrinsic resolution information to construct so-called multi-resolution images.

evidence.loc: The combination in th uv domain
evidence.quote: More importantly, the interferometric ‘negative bowl’ around the bright source in the original Interf image also disappears, increasing the image fidelity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Canonical SED fitting smoothing all bands to 36.3'' resolution was found insufficient to resolve dense cores at 2.8 kpc, motivating the multi-resolution approach.

evidence.loc: Multi-resolution temperature and column density images
evidence.quote: While sufficient for nearby star-forming regions, the method cannot pinpoint dense cores in distant regions (cite: Jiao2025b).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Herschel 70 um data and ATLASGAL 870 um data were excluded from the SED fitting (REweis vs EQweis) because 70 um is contaminated by warm protostellar dust and 870 um is contaminated by CO (3-2) line emission.

evidence.loc: Multi-resolution temperature and column density images
evidence.quote: The 70 $\mu$m data were not used in our fitting due to their potential contamination by hot dust components from protostars.
Besides, the 870 $\mu$m point deviates significantly from the model which is supposed to be contaminated by the CO (3-2) line emission.

limitations_admitted.value: Using an 18''-resolution dust temperature to derive 6.2'' column density smooths temperature gradients and can overestimate column density toward hot evolved sources by ~25% (e.g., 33 K vs 40 K).

evidence.loc: Multi-resolution temperature and column density images
evidence.quote: To give an estimate, at 1.3 mm, adopting the assumed 33 K instead of the true 40 K overestimates the inferred column density by $N_{\rm assu}/N_{\rm true}\sim B_\nu(40\,\mathrm{K})/B_\nu(33\,\mathrm{K})\simeq1.25$, i.e., $\sim25\%$ in the optically thin limit.

limitations_admitted.value: Free-free emission from ionized gas in the evolved southern region can contaminate the 1.3 mm continuum by up to 14% in an 8'' beam.

evidence.loc: Multi-resolution temperature and column density images
evidence.quote: But the corresponding 1.3 mm emission is as bright as 0.53 Jy beam$^{-1}$, so the free-free contamination is at most 14% in an 8$''$ beam.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust opacity model choice (Hildebrand 1983 vs Ossenkopf & Henning 1994) introduces a ~30% systematic uncertainty on absolute column densities and ~9% on dust temperatures.

evidence.quote: Relative to H83, the OH94 assumption yields lower column densities of $27\pm1$% and higher dust temperatures higher of $9\pm1$%. This implies that the absolute values of $N_{\rm H_2}$ and $T_{\rm dust}$ are uncertain at the $\sim$30% level or higher.

limitations_admitted.value: Apparent decrease in minimum fragment mass from young (2.2 M_sun) to evolved (0.6 M_sun) is an observational mass-sensitivity bias caused by warmer dust temperatures in the evolved region.

evidence.quote: In contrast, the apparent decrease in the minimum fragment mass from 2.2 to $0.6~M_\odot$ is unlikely to reflect intrinsic physical evolution but rather arises from observational biases.

referee_caveats_inferred: The multi-resolution column density map has spatially varying resolution (6.2'', 18'', 36.3''), which introduces an artificial break near 18'' (~0.25 pc) in spatial power spectra and Delta-variance and may affect the high-column-density tail of the N-PDF relative to the low-column-density lognormal component.
Dividing the 3 subregions (Young, Intermediate, Evolved) into 2 N-PDF zones (Quiet and Active) splits the Intermediate region in half rather than comparing the three stages directly.
